post.description: :::warning **⚠️ Chat only** This model currently supports chat requests only and has not yet been adapted for agent use. Connecting it to an agent may cause request errors or unexpected results. ::: > Kimi K3 is an OpenAI Responses–compatible endpoint that supports chat, function calling, image input, streaming, and reasoning, with a **1M-token** context window. Reasoning is on by default. `reasoning.effort` can be `low` / `medium` / `high`. Mix text and images in a single message. Custom function calling, with optional JSON-constrained answers. Use the unified /openai/v1/responses endpoint with model set to kimi-k3. ## Reasoning The model **reasons by default**. Higher `reasoning.effort` means more thorough reasoning and possibly higher latency. - `low`: faster - `medium`: balanced - `high`: more thorough, better for complex questions If omitted, the model chooses. Reasoning summaries are for display only and do not need to be sent back as input. :::warning This model **does not support** web search. Built-in tools such as `web_search` are ignored. ::: ## Tools and input ```json { "model": "kimi-k3", "stream": true, "input": "Introduce Beijing in one sentence" } ``` ```json { "model": "kimi-k3", "stream": false, "instructions": "Answer in English only", "input": [ { "role": "user", "content": "My name is Xiaoming" }, { "role": "assistant", "content": "Hi Xiaoming." }, { "role": "user", "content": "What is my name?" } ] } ``` ```json { "model": "kimi-k3", "stream": true, "reasoning": { "effort": "high" }, "input": "Which is larger, 9.11 or 9.9?" } ``` Declare functions the model can call. Only `function` tools are supported. After you pass `tools`, set `tool_choice` to `auto` to let the model decide, or pass an object to pin a specific function. Do not send `tool_choice` if you are not sending `tools`. ```json { "model": "kimi-k3", "stream": false, "input": "What's the weather like in Shanghai right now?", "tool_choice": "auto", "tools": [ { "type": "function", "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get the current weather for a city", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "city": { "type": "string", "description": "City name" } }, "required": ["city"], "additionalProperties": false } } ] } ``` The model returns a `function_call`. After you run the function, append both that item and your `function_call_output` to `input`, paired by `call_id`: ```json { "model": "kimi-k3", "stream": false, "tools": [ { "type": "function", "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get the current weather for a city", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "city": { "type": "string", "description": "City name" } }, "required": ["city"], "additionalProperties": false } } ], "input": [ { "role": "user", "content": "What's the weather like in Beijing right now?" }, { "type": "function_call", "call_id": "call_6102a526bdda4ebf8e982aa3", "name": "get_weather", "arguments": "{\"city\":\"Beijing\"}" }, { "type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "call_6102a526bdda4ebf8e982aa3", "output": "{\"temp_c\":21,\"condition\":\"sunny\"}" } ] } ``` Set `text.format` to constrain the answer to JSON: ```json { "text": { "format": { "type": "json_object" } } } ``` Use `json_schema` to validate the answer against your own schema. ```json { "model": "kimi-k3", "stream": false, "input": "Give information about Tokyo", "text": { "format": { "type": "json_schema", "name": "city_info", "strict": true, "schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "city": { "type": "string" }, "country": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["city", "country"], "additionalProperties": false } } } } ``` Mix `input_image` and `input_text` parts in the same message. `image_url` can be a publicly reachable image URL or `data:image/{format};base64,{data}`: ```json { "model": "kimi-k3", "stream": false, "input": [ { "role": "user", "content": [ { "type": "input_text", "text": "What's in this image?" }, { "type": "input_image", "image_url": "https://example.com/cat.png" } ] } ] } ``` ## Error handling Check the response body, not only the HTTP status. Errors are returned either as `{"code": ..., "msg": "..."}` (for example 401 invalid API key, 402 insufficient credits, 429 rate limited; the HTTP status may still be 200) or as `{"error": {"type": "...", "message": "..."}}`.

input.description: Input can be a string or an array. Each array item is a message, a function call, or a function result.

oneOf.title: message
oneOf.description: A message object with role and content. `type` is optional and defaults to `message`.

type.description: Message type. Optional; defaults to `message` if omitted.

role.description: Role of the message author. `system` and `developer` instructions take priority over `user`. `assistant` is a previous reply.

content.description: Message content. A string, or an array of text and image parts. Images are only allowed on `user` messages.

oneOf.title: input_image
oneOf.description: Image part. Only allowed on `user` messages. Common formats such as PNG and JPEG are supported.

image_url.description: Image URL. A publicly reachable URL, or a `data:image/{format};base64,{data}` string. The link must be directly downloadable, otherwise the request returns 400.

oneOf.title: function_call
oneOf.description: A function call the model made in the previous turn. Pair it with `function_call_output` by `call_id`.

call_id.description: Call ID. Send back the `call_id` from the previous output as-is.

name.description: Name of the function the model called.

arguments.description: Function arguments as a JSON string.

oneOf.title: function_call_output
oneOf.description: Function result to send back to the model.

call_id.description: Call ID. Must match the corresponding `function_call`.

output.description: Function result as text. Serialize structured results to a JSON string first.

instructions.description: System instructions for the model, inserted as a system message before `input`.

stream.description: When true, the response is streamed as server-sent events. When false, the full response is returned after completion. Defaults to true.

reasoning.description: Reasoning settings. Reasoning is on by default.

effort.description: Reasoning effort. Higher values reason more thoroughly and may add latency. Allowed: `low`, `medium`, `high`. If omitted, the model chooses.

items.title: function
items.description: A function the model can call. After the model requests a call, you run it and send the result back as `function_call_output`.

name.description: Function name. Returned as-is when the model calls it.

description.description: What the function does. Helps the model decide when to call it.
examples: Get the current weather for a city

parameters.description: Function parameter definition as a JSON Schema object.

strict.description: Whether to generate arguments strictly from `parameters`.

tools.description: Optional list of tools the model can call. Only `function` is supported. Built-in tools such as `web_search` are ignored.

tool_choice.description: Tool choice. When `tools` is set, use `auto` to let the model decide, or pass an object to pin a function. Do not send this field if `tools` is not set.

oneOf.title: Auto
oneOf.description: Preset strategy. `auto` lets the model decide whether to call a function.

name.description: Function name. Returned as-is when the model calls it.

format.title: text.format
format.description: Format the answer should follow. Plain text if omitted.

oneOf.title: json_object
oneOf.description: JSON mode. The model outputs a valid JSON object. Describe the expected structure in the prompt.

oneOf.title: json_schema
oneOf.description: Structured output. The model emits JSON that follows your schema.

strict.description: Whether to validate the answer strictly against the schema. Only applies to `json_schema`. When `true`, set `additionalProperties: false` and list every field in `required`.

schema.description: JSON Schema the answer must follow. Required when `type` is `json_schema`.

200.description: Success. `stream=true` (default) returns `text/event-stream`; `stream=false` returns `application/json`. Pre-check failures also return HTTP 200 — use `code` to tell them apart.

oneOf.description: Final response object. Returned directly when `stream=false`; carried on the `response.completed` event when streaming.

created_at.description: Creation time as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

status.description: Response status. `completed` on success. `in_progress` only appears on the `response.created` event.

model.description: Identifier of the model that served the request.

output.description: Output items in order. Usually a reasoning summary, then a reply and/or function calls.

oneOf.title: reasoning
oneOf.description: Reasoning summary for this turn. For display only; do not send it back as input.

text.description: Generated text. If JSON output is enabled, this is a JSON string.

annotations.description: Citations. Always an empty array for this model.

oneOf.title: function_call
oneOf.description: A function the model wants to call. After you run it, send back a `function_call_output` with the same `call_id`.

arguments.description: Call arguments as a JSON string.

call_id.description: Call ID. Use this when sending a `function_call_output`.

input_tokens.description: Input token count, including the prompt, instructions, history, images, and function definitions.

output_tokens.description: Output token count, including tokens used for reasoning.

input_tokens_details.description: Input token breakdown. Returned when a cache hit occurs.

credits_consumed.description: Non-streaming: credits_consumed is a top-level field. Streaming: it is on the response.completed event, next to type.

oneOf.title: Success response

oneOf.description: Pre-check failed (auth, balance, rate limit, or parameter format). HTTP status is still 200 — use `code` to tell.

code.description: Business error code: `401` missing or invalid API key; `402` insufficient balance; `429` too many requests; `400` / `422` invalid parameters; `500` internal error.

examples: Credits insufficient : Your current balance isn’t enough to run this request. Please top up to continue.

oneOf.title: Pre-check failed

schema.description: A full response on success. Pre-check failures (parameters, auth, and similar) also return HTTP 200 — use `code` to tell them apart.

summary.text: The user wants a one-sentence introduction to Beijing…

content.text: Beijing is China's capital, a historic city with more than three thousand years of urban history, home to landmarks such as the Forbidden City and the Great Wall, and a modern international metropolis.

summary.text: The user asked about the weather in Shanghai, so call get_weather.

value.msg: Credits insufficient : Your current balance isn’t enough to run this request. Please top up to continue.
The api key does not exist.
Your call frequency is too high. Please try again later.

error.message: Server exception, please try again later
The server is currently being maintained, please try again later~

400.description: The model rejected the request, for example because an image URL could not be downloaded.

schema.description: Returned when generation fails before any content is produced. HTTP status is non-2xx.

429.description: Service is at capacity. Try again later.

schema.description: Returned when generation fails before any content is produced. HTTP status is non-2xx.
Returned when generation fails before any content is produced. HTTP status is non-2xx.

502.description: Service is temporarily unavailable. Try again later.

schema.description: Returned when generation fails before any content is produced. HTTP status is non-2xx.

BearerAuth.description: All API requests require a Bearer Token. Add the header `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY` to authenticate requests.
